paragraphs: How a Rice Cooker Works, posted by Leo. On Saturday morning, the Explorers went to a cooking class. Chef Lucy asked, "How does a cooker know that the rice is ready?" I said, "A small cook lives inside!" Chef Lucy laughed, and then she explained the real answer. Here is my diagram of an electric rice cooker. It is simple, but it is correct.

Look at the diagram and read the four labels. Label one is the lid. It keeps the steam inside. Label two is the pot. The rice and the water go in the pot. Label three is the heater. It is under the pot, and it is electric. It uses electricity from the wall. The pot is metal, and it gets hot fast. Label four is the switch. It turns off the heater at the right time.

Now follow the steps. First, put one cup of rice and two cups of water in the pot. Then close the lid and push the switch down. The heater gets hot, and the water begins to boil. The rice takes the water, so the water gets less. When the water is gone, the pot gets hotter. Then the switch jumps up, and the heater turns off. So the cooker knows by itself that the rice is ready. The rice is ready in about twenty minutes.

The cooking class has a big kitchen with simple furniture. There are two long tables and twelve stools. The room is clean and big. After the lesson, Chef Lucy offered us a bowl of rice with vegetables. The meal was soft and hot, and it was very healthy. We ate it at the long tables. Mia asked for more, and Chef Lucy offered her a second bowl.

A cooker is hot, so do not touch the pot. Water and electricity are a bad mix. If you want to open the lid, use a cloth. Ask an adult to help you. Does your family have a rice cooker at home? Tell us about it in a message!
